thread:
Sarah L: incident-bot paged oncall for SEV2: High error rate on generation endpoints in us-west-2. RequestID samples included in the alert.
incident-bot: Pager details: cpu_surge > 85% for model-serv-03, 504 errors spike, error_rate 18% over baseline. Playbook: https://redwood/internal/playbooks/serving-error-response
Mike C: Acknowledged. I'm oncall.
Leila R: Thanks Mike. Any ETA on root cause? Is this a model load, KV cache, or infra flapping?
Mike C: Initial look: node mem pressure on model-serv-03, OOM kills reported at 20:14 UTC. Rolling restart in progress on the pool.
Omar T: Copy. Are we seeing customer-facing 504/429s or degraded latencies only? Need to classify impact for paging severity justification.
Mike C: Mostly 504s with partial success for small inputs. 3 customers reported elevated error rates via support. I set page to SEV2 because multiple customers affected and sustained errors >5m.
Jenny P: Noted. I'm pulling support tickets and routing to PMs. Which tenants are impacted?
Mike C: Tenants A and C have requests hitting the affected cluster. Tenant A had a larger traffic spike due to a scheduled batch job.
Leila R: Can we mitigate by shifting traffic via smart routing to model-serv-04 in us-west-2? Or fall back to a quantized variant in another pool?
Mike C: Doing a canary route: added model-serv-04 and enabled fallback to quantized-v1 for non-sensitive routes. Command run:
```
redwood route update --from model-serv-03 --to model-serv-04 --weight 0.6 --fallback quantized-v1
```
incident-bot: Routing update: 60% shifted to model-serv-04, fallback quantized-v1 enabled. Monitor latency and errors.
Leila R: Observability shows error rate dropping to 6% after shifting. Still some residual 504s likely from in-flight KV cache inconsistencies.
Mike C: Restarted model-serv-03 processes gracefully and cleared local KV cache. Will monitor for recurrence.
Sarah L: Customer impact estimate: ~4% of total requests in us-west-2 during window; 3 customers reported errors, 1 with sporadic data-loss concern (false negatives on re-rank).
Omar T: Please add that to the incident summary for the post-incident triage. We need severity classification and whether this maps to SEV1 for SLAs.
Jenny P: From support: Tenant A marked performance degradation, no data loss confirmed. They want a postmortem and action items. I'll schedule a post-incident call.
Mike C: Current status: errors down to 1.5%, latency within SLO for routed hosts. Holding mitigation will be to re-balance traffic and keep fallback enabled for 2 hours.
Leila R: Root cause hypothesis: KV cache eviction storm due to simultaneous restarts + larger batch requests that exceed prefix caching window. Need reproduction test in staging.
Mike C: Agreed. I can reproduce with the batch job in a staging cutoff. I'll open a repro issue with steps and logs.
Sarah L: For immediate next steps: 1) Stabilize routing (Mike), 2) Repro in staging (Mike/Leila), 3) Postmortem & action items (Jenny/Product), 4) Customer comms (Jenny/Support)
Jenny P: Setting postmortem meeting for tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Thread for follow-ups: I'll create an incident tracker.
product-bot: Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-03-10T16:00:00Z. Calendar invite sent.
Omar T: For the postmortem, we should scope action items by severity and estimated effort: Severity = S2 but customer impact tier = Tier 2 (high revenue customer flagged). That means at least one P1 action (mitigation automation) and several P2s.
Leila R: Proposed action items (short list):
- Action 1: Add automated KV cache warmup + safe-evict policy to prevent eviction storms. Owner: Leila. Est size: 3 engineer-days (P1)
- Action 2: Improve routing fallback granularity to avoid cross-tenant imbalance. Owner: Mike. Est size: 2 engineer-days (P2)
- Action 3: Add alerting for batch job spikes per tenant with circuit-breaker. Owner: Omar. Est size: 2 engineer-days (P2)
- Action 4: Customer post-incident report and SLA review. Owner: Jenny. Est size: 1 engineer-day (P2)
- Action 5: Staging reproducibility harness for KV cache + large-batch. Owner: Mike/Leila. Est size: 4 engineer-days (P2)
Mike C: I'm fine with those. I'll create GH issues and include reproduction snippet and logs. Label with "incident-2105554321".
Jenny P: When assigning priorities for quarterly planning, P1 action should be scheduled into the next sprint immediately. P2 items go into the remediation backlog and targeted Q2 iterations.
Omar T: For sprint planning, estimate costs: P1 (3 dev-days) -> can be burnt in an on-call week or scheduled with small squad. P2 items combined ~9 dev-days, we can phase across two sprints.
Sarah L: Please include acceptance criteria in the GH issues: e.g., for KV cache automation: no eviction storms in a 24h synthetic spike test and no customer errors in 2 repeated runs.
Leila R: I'll draft the test harness and the runbook steps for rollback. Also adding a canary metric to the console dashboard.
Jenny P: Created incident tracker: https://redwood/incidents/2105554321. GH issues:
- GH#6421 Add KV safe-evict policy (assignee: Leila R)
- GH#6422 Routing fallback granularity (assignee: Mike C)
- GH#6423 Tenant spike alerting + circuit breaker (assignee: Omar T)
- GH#6424 Post-incident customer report (assignee: Jenny P)
- GH#6425 Staging repro harness (assignees: Mike C, Leila R)
Mike C: Marking GH issues as P1/P2 and linking to the postmortem calendar item.
incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Duration: 27m.
Sarah L: Postmortem owner? Recommend Leila + Mike co-author; Jenny will add customer comms section.
Jenny P: I'll take responsibility to close the incident tracker once GH issues have acceptance criteria and owners are confirmed.
Omar T: One more note for prioritization scoring: customer revenue tier and SLA hit should bump P1 urgency. Please add that rationale in GH#6421 comment.
Leila R: Noted. I'll add technical design with mockups and rollout plan. Est rollout: canary -> 50% -> 100% over 48h.
Mike C: After postmortem we should add a long-term action: parameterize eviction thresholds per model family; that's R&D scope but worth tagging R&D backlog.
Jenny P: Thanks team. I'll circulate the postmortem template pre-meeting and collect logs + timeline. Please upload any logs to the tracker before 14:00 UTC tomorrow.
Sarah L: Closing notes: Good mitigation handoff. We reduced customer impact quickly. Postmortem will determine whether this requires a process change in release/runbook.
Mike C: Logging done. Will follow up in GH.
Jenny P: Closing the thread for now — we'll resume in the postmortem call.
